next_candidate.implementation: Read maxBufferSize from cached Vulkan1.3 properties. Bound the requirements probe and plan block-aligned host buffer windows that contain the complete requested guest span. Coarse address-space entries become checked hints, not assertions of whole-page coverage. Keep stable original BDA ownership per physical backing range. Bind existing backing to new overlapping windows and future backing allocations to every overlapping window; no truncation, replacement values or forced guest work omission. Enable sparseResidencyAliased only when supported and mark sparse buffers accordingly. Add a command-buffer memory dependency for alias identities, not a host/device-idle wait. Prevent u32 overflow in large physical allocation size/BDA loop and split DMA uploads into representable chunks.
next_candidate.limitations: A single requested aligned span larger than the device buffer limit is refused explicitly rather than silently clipped; segmentation of a genuinely larger single shader resource is not implemented here. Hosts without sparseResidencyAliased can use disjoint windows but cannot create overlapping views in this candidate. Alias barriers are conservative once overlapping views exist and may require later performance refinement. Runtime compatibility/performance is not yet demonstrated.
